species.real: Hellbenders have been nicknamed 'snot otters' and 'lasagna lizards' for the slimy, ruffled skin folds that let them absorb oxygen from the water.
species.name: Hellbendlet

dex.text: A flat, wrinkly, unbothered thing under a rock in the creek. Breathes through its skin and judges you through its very small eyes.
dex.fact: The eastern hellbender is North America's biggest salamander. It breathes mostly through the folds of its skin, so it needs clean, cold, fast-flowing water.

species.real: A male hellbender digs a nest under a flat rock and guards the eggs, which hatch with him still on watch.
species.name: Hellbender

dex.text: Two feet of wrinkles and patience. Local names include snot otter and devil dog, and it has heard all of them.
dex.fact: Hellbenders can live for decades. They have declined where streams are dammed, silted or polluted, so a healthy population is a sign of a healthy river.
